accessibility.title: Accessibility Statement
accessibility.intro: This statement describes the accessibility status of riccardobozzato.com. The goal is a site usable by everyone, regardless of disability or assistive technology.

sections.title: 1. Conformance Status
sections.content:
Partially conformant. The site was self-assessed and manually reviewed on 2 October 2026 against WCAG 2.2 level AA.

Most content and components meet the criteria. Known exceptions are listed in section 5 and are limited to third-party components I do not control.

sections.title: 2. Applicable Standards
sections.content:
The site is evaluated against:

WCAG 2.2, Web Content Accessibility Guidelines, level AA (W3C Recommendation, October 2023)
Italian Law 13 March 1988 no. 104 and subsequent amendments, articles 55 onwards
AgID guidelines for the measurability and monitoring of web accessibility (2021)
European Accessibility Act, transposed in Italy, applicable to e-commerce services

sections.title: 3. Criteria Applied
sections.content: All level A and AA criteria of WCAG 2.2 were reviewed. In particular the criteria covering structure and orientation (1.3.1, 1.3.2), text alternatives (1.1.1), minimum contrast (1.4.3, 1.4.11), keyboard navigation (2.1.1, 2.1.2, 2.4.1, 2.4.3, 2.4.7), changes of context (3.2.1, 3.2.2, 3.2.3, 3.2.4), accessible name and role (4.1.2), status messages (4.1.3) and ARIA landmarks (2.4.1).

sections.title: 4. Measures Implemented
sections.content:
Semantic structure with identified header, nav, main and footer; a 'Skip to main content' link as the first focusable element.

Consistent heading hierarchy on every page, with no skipped levels.

Colour contrast verified against the real theme, not only the default one.

All interactive controls are reachable and operable by keyboard, with a focus indicator that is always visible.

Decorative icons marked aria-hidden; meaningful icons carry alternative text.

Forms with explicit labels, required states declared, and error messages associated to their input via aria-describedby.

Status messages (form submission, loading) announced with role=status or aria-live.

Dynamic content (response messages) announced without moving focus.

Reduced motion: animations respect prefers-reduced-motion and the cookie banner can be printed without interference.

Selectable text and 200% zoom without loss of content or functionality, including on mobile.

No information conveyed by colour alone.

sections.title: 5. Partial Conformance - Known Limitations
sections.content:
Cookie banner: while the consent window is open, the underlying content remains in the document flow because the banner does not use a modal dialog that traps navigation. Some screen reader users may need to dismiss it explicitly to reach the content.

Third-party advertising: the content and behaviour of ads depend on Google AdSense and are outside my control. They are not always labelled as advertising in an accessible way and may not meet the required contrast. They appear only if you accept the advertising category.

Amazon affiliate links: visually labelled, but the textual indication for screen reader users is not always complete.

Netlify Identity widget: the third-party script is also loaded on public pages, where it is never used. It introduces no visible content or focus traps, but it does add an unnecessary network request.

sections.title: 6. Techniques Used
sections.content:
Semantic HTML with ARIA landmarks; role and aria-* attributes only where native markup is insufficient.

Visible focus that is never removed, managed with :focus-visible so mouse users are not penalised.

Support for prefers-reduced-motion, prefers-contrast and forced-colors where applicable.

No text baked into images: information is always available as real, selectable, indexable text.

sections.title: 7. Assessment Tools
sections.content:
Lighthouse Accessibility (Chrome), axe DevTools and WAVE, run on the main pages in both Italian and English.

Manual keyboard verification across all flows: navigation, services page, contact form, playbook download and the cookie panel.

This check is part of the definition of 'done' for every change, alongside TypeScript and ESLint at build time.

sections.title: 8. Feedback and Contact
sections.content: If you find an accessibility problem, write to riccardobozzato@gmail.com with the page, the problem and, if possible, the assistive technology you use. I reply within 5 business days and, when the problem affects a shared component, the fix goes into the next development cycle.

sections.title: 9. Remediation Process
sections.content:
Reports are logged with the page, the WCAG criterion involved and the impact. Issues that block reading or use of content take top priority and are fixed before any new feature.

If you consider the response inadequate you can lodge a complaint with AgID or the Italian Data Protection Authority.

sections.title: 10. Updating This Statement
sections.content: This statement is reviewed at least once a year, and whenever site content, structure or components change significantly. The date at the top always reflects the latest review. Substantial changes are announced on the home page.

accessibility.description: Accessibility statement for riccardobozzato.com: WCAG 2.2 level AA conformance, measures taken and known limitations.

Head of Operations at Ciao Elsa (2026). PMP® certified. Now I help digital teams scale without imploding.

home.servicesSubtitle: Four ways to bring order to your operations.

serviceList.title: Delivery & Process Design
serviceList.desc: Agile, Scrum, Kanban — but tailored to your team, not copied from a textbook. Release planning, capacity management, risk mitigation for teams of 8-12. 20-40% faster time-to-market.

projects.title: What I have run
projects.subtitle: Seven years in operations: retail, B2B e-commerce, consulting. Below is the full path, plus the projects where you can check the result yourself.
projects.trackSubtitle: Four companies, the same question every time: why does this team take thirty days to do something that should take three?

track.scope: Where I learned what happens when a process is not written down: in retail, the deadline does not move.
track.outcome: Rules and flows made repeatable across stores and warehouse

track.scope: A chain with high volumes and thin margins: here, two points of efficiency is the entire margin.
First client projects, with the stated goal of removing manual steps and waiting time.
A €500K portfolio across Magento, Shopware and Pimcore, with distributed teams of 8-12. Here I introduced Agile to an organisation that did not use it.

projects.clientSubtitle: One project, told in full. It is the only one where you can check my work yourself.

panificio.title: Panificio da Sergio
panificio.subtitle: E-commerce for a family bakery, delivered and still online
panificio.description: Nobody asked me for a website. They had a recipe archive handwritten on paper, three generations who disagreed about everything, and a shop that ended each day not knowing what it had sold. The real work was deciding what to automate and what to leave to a human.
panificio.problem: Three generations with incompatible opinions on pricing, catalogue and opening hours. No data on what actually sold, because it was recorded by hand. A website with a £0 materials budget.
approach: A workshop with all three generations together, so principles were decided before specs
Specs written in Italian and English, so nobody could claim they had not understood
Open source and free tiers only: the budget constraint became the design constraint
A catalogue with collection scheduling, because for bread the date matters more than the price
outcome: A complete e-commerce site in production, under the materials budget
End-to-end order flow: catalogue, cart, collection, confirmation, dashboard
Bilingual, with care for the shop's walk-in customers
Still online months later, which is the only test that counts
panificio.stackNote: Next.js, Tailwind, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, next-intl, Netlify

built.title: Synapse

built.reach: 9,000+ notes indexed, each with an embedding and a link
built.lesson: It is where everything I learn about processes ends up. If I do not write it there, I forget it, and what I forget is the definition of tribal knowledge.

services.title: From chaos to predictable execution in 30 days

items.q: How do payment and invoicing work?
items.a: After the free call you get a written proposal with scope, timeline and fixed price. Bank transfer: 100% for the Audit, 50/50 for the Overhaul. I issue an invoice with withholding tax (occasional service).

items.q: How much of my team's time do you need?

Start with the Audit: it tells you if and where to act. Small teams often need just Audit + Template Pack, no Overhaul.

items.q: Do you work in Italian or English?
items.a: Both. I've worked with distributed teams in two languages; docs and training in your team's language.
You get the roadmap and decide: implement it yourself, implement it together with the Overhaul (the Audit cost is deducted), or do nothing. No pressure.

freebie.title: Time-to-Market Diagnostic
freebie.subtitle: Ninety minutes, one worksheet, three actions with a name and a date.
freebie.description: This is the worksheet I use to find out where a team loses time, before deciding what to fix. You fill it in three steps: describe the process, separate the time someone is genuinely working from the time the work is waiting, then cross two numbers to reach a decision. If ninety minutes don't produce three actions with an owner, the worksheet failed.
freebie.honestNote: It contains no universal benchmarks. The thresholds are sensible defaults to get you reasoning: change them when you have your own data that contradicts them.
whatsInside: Three steps on a single process at a time, with the time budget for each
The three things to count: handoffs, tools involved, approvals
The efficiency calculation, and the threshold below which a process is pure waiting
The four causes waiting time comes from, in the order you should look for them
A four-quadrant matrix that ends in a decision rather than a wish
Three actions with an owner, a deadline, and the number that tells you it worked

how.title: Pick one process
how.desc: The one that makes you miss promises most often. Not the easiest to measure: that is a trap.

how.title: Fill it in away from your desk
how.desc: Ninety minutes with the whiteboard open. Numbers from memory are worthless: if you cannot say where a number came from, it does not count.

how.title: Decide and write it down
how.desc: Three actions, not seven. A list of seven never starts. Put a name and a date next to each one.

forWho: Heads of Operations, Operations Managers and Delivery Managers
Project Managers and Scrum Masters who answer for deadlines
Founders and COOs of a scale-up that outgrew its processes
E-commerce Managers answerable for fulfilment and returns
forWhoNot: If you want a course to follow: there is no video here, just a sheet to fill in
If you have fewer than ten people and a single process: there is no chaos to diagnose yet
If you want someone to do it for you: that is consulting, and it costs
If you want software to do it for you: it exists, and it is nothing like what you do

about.title: About Riccardo
about.subtitle: Operations & Delivery. PMP®. From retail to Head of Operations — with measurable results along the way.
about.intro: Delivery Manager & Head of Operations (PMP®). 7+ years making teams faster and less chaotic. Enterprise portfolio €500K+, teams of 8-12, 40% faster time-to-market. Started in retail, moved through Accenture, led operations at Ciao Elsa. PMP® certified. Now looking for the next challenge — if your team needs operational order, let's talk.
story: My career started in retail management — In’s Mercato, Aldi, Terranova. I learned operations the hard way: managing inventory, scheduling shifts, coaching teams, explaining to the regional manager why we missed target. It was the best possible training for delivery management, even if I didn’t know it yet.

Then Accenture. I built enterprise applications (SAP UI5, JavaScript) and automated processes that had been manual for years: +30% efficiency, -15% administrative errors, -20% response times. It was the first time I saw that the right process beats raw talent — every time.

At Esse Solutions I owned a €500K portfolio of digital projects, coordinating distributed teams of 8-12 across B2B eCommerce (Magento, Shopware) and PIM/DAM (Pimcore). I introduced structured Agile where there was none: productivity went up 25%, time-to-market dropped 40%, completion times shrank 20%.

At Ciao Elsa I was Head of Operations for 8 weeks — by design. The startup needed an operations function from scratch: processes, KPIs, team structure, governance. I built it, handed it over, and left. A short engagement that proved the approach works even at startup speed.

I'm currently in transition — my Ciao Elsa engagement has concluded and I'm open to new opportunities. I bring a strong track record: operational architectures built in both enterprise and startup environments, PMP® certification, and the conviction that the right process beats raw talent — every time. In the meantime, I build tools (ShipKit, VulnClaw) because you can't design good systems if you've never built anything.
about.philosophy: Most companies don't fail because they lack talent or ideas. They fail because their operations can't handle the weight of their own growth. I build the operating system that fixes that — combining the rigor of PMP® with the speed of someone who's been in the trenches. No jargon. No theater. Just systems that work.
about.ctaDesc: Have a project, idea, or just want to chat? I'm always open to interesting conversations.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This notice explains how we handle personal data from visitors to riccardobozzato.com. The site has no profiling purpose and does not require an account to be browsed.

sections.title: 1. Data Controller
sections.content:
Controller: Riccardo Bozzato, based in Legnaro (PD), Italy.
Contact for any data-related question: riccardobozzato@gmail.com.
The site is hosted on Netlify and distributed through Cloudflare (CDN and DNS). Both process technical data such as IP address and user agent to serve the site.

sections.title: 2. Data Collected - Per Service
sections.content:
General contact form: name, email and message. Used for job applications, project enquiries or consulting.

Consulting services (Operational Audit, Operations Overhaul, Fractional Head of Operations): name, email, company, description of the operational problem, team and process details. For the Overhaul we may need platform details (Magento, Shopware, Pimcore) and temporary access credentials, destroyed at the end of the engagement. Prices are agreed on a call and in the written proposal: no rate is published on the site.

Free resource downloads (playbook): name and email address, used to deliver the PDF and send the email sequence (maximum 6 emails in 30 days). Double opt-in applies: without address confirmation the sequence does not start.

CV download: no data collected, the download is anonymous.

ShipKit purchase: name, email and billing address, handled by Stripe. I never receive or store your card details.

sections.title: 3. How I Use Your Data
sections.content:
I use data to answer enquiries, deliver agreed services and, only if you requested the playbook, send you the operations email sequence. I do not sell your data, do not share it with third parties for marketing and do not use it to train models.

Playbook leads are stored on Netlify Blobs, a store located in the United States.

sections.title: 4. Cookies, Analytics and Advertising
sections.content:
The site separates three categories and you choose which to accept.

Necessary: always active. They make the site work (session language, rate limiting, double opt-in and unsubscribe tokens) and cannot be disabled.

Analytics: Google Analytics 4, loaded only after your explicit consent. It runs with IP anonymization and with Google's advertising signals disabled unless you also accepted the advertising category. It tells me which pages get read.

Advertising: Google AdSense and its partners may set cookies to serve relevant ads and measure campaigns. These are also loaded only with your consent. The site may also host directly sold sponsored content, always labelled as such.

If you decline, neither GA4 nor AdSense is requested: the site works normally, without measurement or ads.

sections.title: 5. Consent, Double Opt-In and Unsubscribing
sections.content:
The legal basis is your consent, given through an affirmative action. The email sequence uses double opt-in: you receive a confirmation email and the sequence starts only after you click the confirmation link.

Every email in the sequence contains an unsubscribe link that acts immediately. You can also change your cookie choices at any time, via the 'Cookie settings' link in the site footer.

Consent is never a condition of purchase.

sections.title: 6. Legal Basis (GDPR)
sections.content:
Art. 6.1.a Consent: non-essential cookies, email sequence.
Art. 6.1.b Performance of a contract: replies to contact requests and services in progress.
Art. 6.1.c Legal obligation: billing data, retained for 10 years as required by tax law.
Art. 6.1.f Legitimate interest: site security (rate limiting, technical logs) and defence against abuse.

sections.title: 7. Data Retention
sections.content:
Contact requests and applications: 24 months from last contact, unless longer retention is legally required.
Billing data: 10 years (tax obligation).
Playbook sequence leads: 30 days after the last email, then deleted. If you unsubscribe, they are deleted immediately.
Technical security logs: 90 days.
Technical credentials provided for an Overhaul engagement: destroyed at the end of the engagement.

sections.title: 8. Your Rights (GDPR)
sections.content:
You can ask at any time for access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability and objection, and you can withdraw consent.
To exercise them write to riccardobozzato@gmail.com. I reply within 30 days.
I apply no automated decision-making and no profiling. You can request your data in JSON format.

sections.title: 9. Third Parties and Processors
sections.content:
Only strictly necessary services, with the related processing:

Netlify (Netlify Inc., USA): hosting, Netlify Identity for admin area authentication, and Netlify Blobs for playbook lead storage.
Cloudflare (Cloudflare Inc., USA): CDN, DNS, attack mitigation and edge content delivery.
Google Ireland Limited (Ireland, with transfers to the USA): Google Analytics 4 and, if you accepted, Google AdSense.
Resend Inc. (USA): transactional and sequence email delivery.
Stripe Inc. (USA): payments, for the ShipKit purchase only.
Amazon EU S.a.r.l.: affiliate programme. Some outbound links are affiliate links and earn a commission. No additional tracking cookies are used for the affiliation.

sections.title: 10. International Transfers
sections.content:
Netlify, Cloudflare, Resend, Stripe and Google process data outside the European Economic Area. These transfers rely on the European Commission's Standard Contractual Clauses, Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2021/914, plus supplementary measures such as IP anonymization in Google Analytics.
You can request a copy of the applicable SCCs by writing to riccardobozzato@gmail.com.

sections.title: 11. Data Security
sections.content:
HTTPS with TLS sitewide, HSTS with a two-year max-age, a restrictive CSP, rate limiting on every API and fail-closed behaviour on all protected endpoints. Secrets are never committed to the repository and admin passwords are never hardcoded in source.
No system is breach-proof: in the event of a data breach I will notify you by email without undue delay and with the information required by the GDPR.

sections.title: 12. Third-party cookies and scripts
sections.content:
Netlify Identity: the authentication script is loaded on every page of the site, even though it is only used in the /login reserved area. It handles the session and may set technical cookies. No profiling cookies are set.

Google Tag Manager: the GTM-5XPLS93 container is injected by the Cloudflare CDN, not by this site's code, and is requested on every visit. I can disclose this but not directly control it: whoever manages that configuration can either remove it or make it respect consent.

Google Fonts: fonts are served from fonts.gstatic.com, with the implied consequence that your IP address is sent to Google when the page loads. Fonts are served even if you refuse the analytics and advertising categories, because the page needs them to render.

sections.title: 13. Job Application Data
sections.content: Applications you send are processed to assess the role and, if successful, to manage the employment relationship. I do not share your application data with third parties and do not use it for marketing. You can request erasure at any time.

sections.title: 14. Limitations of Liability
sections.content: Site content, including estimates, metrics and case study results, is for information only and does not constitute legal, tax or financial advice. The user is responsible for decisions taken on the basis of the published information.

sections.title: 15. Changes to This Policy
sections.content: This notice may be updated, for example when new services, new technical partners or regulatory changes require it. The date at the top always reflects the latest revision. Substantial changes are notified by email to anyone who requested the playbook.

sections.title: 16. Complaints
sections.content: If you believe processing infringes the GDPR, you can lodge a complaint with the Italian Data Protection Authority (www.garanteprivacy.it) or with the supervisory authority of your country of residence. You can always write to riccardobozzato@gmail.com first: I reply within 30 days.

advertise.formatsDesc: Starting prices for a single campaign. Get in touch for multi-period packages, dedicated content or the newsletter.

formats.title: Sponsored article
formats.desc: One blog post, written in my editorial voice and technically reviewed by me. No over-sold copy: if the product does not fit, I say no.

formats.title: Newsletter + blog
formats.desc: The best CPM package: one email to the operations sequence list plus one blog post, cross-linked.

formats.title: README sponsorship
formats.desc: Your logo and message in the README of one of my open source projects. Public, permanent, and seen by everyone who uses it.

advertise.pricingNote: Prices exclude VAT. I do not sell generic display banners: the audience is too niche for rotating ads, and that would be noise for both of us.

process.desc: You tell me your product and the goal of the campaign.
You get format, dates, price and a draft of the editorial angle.
Final check and go live. Nothing ships without my approval.
Real campaign metrics: impressions, clicks, CTR and leads generated.

faq.a: The text and the editorial angle are mine. Your product is described accurately, without over-selling: my credibility is worth more than a click.

faq.q: Will you only promote products you recommend?
faq.a: Yes. I turn partnerships down regularly: the wrong partner damages the site more than the fee earns you. I tell you straight away if your product is not a fit.
Every campaign gets a UTM-tagged link. I send the numbers at the end: impressions, clicks, CTR and, if you wire up a form, the leads collected.
Yes, with at least two weeks notice. Blog posts stay online permanently, so the value is not limited to one week.

finalCta.title: Let's talk about your product
finalCta.desc: Tell me what you sell and to whom. I reply within two business days with a proposal.
